transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I'm just tired all the time, and I've no energy. It's been getting worse and I don't feel like myself.
When did you first notice it?
It came on gradually, over about two months now. I can't put my finger on an exact day, it just crept up on me.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's there all day, but it's definitely worse in the afternoon. I've started needing a nap most days, which I never used to do.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
Just a heavy, worn-out feeling, like I've got nothing left in the tank. Not sleepy exactly, just no energy at all.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's not in one spot, it's my whole body really — just a general heaviness all over. I do get a sore shoulder, but that's an old thing I take ibuprofen for.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'd say my energy's only about a 3 out of 10. I've had to give up my swimming — I was going twice a week and I just can't manage it now.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It's there all the time, it doesn't really come and go. It's just always there, though it's worse by the afternoon.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?

Yes, I get more short of breath than usual going up hills, and a couple of friends have said I look pale. I sleep about seven hours but still wake up unrefreshed, and I suppose my mood's a bit flat with all the caring.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had type 2 diabetes for about 12 years now, and I've got an underactive thyroid as well. So I'm on regular medication for both of those.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I take metformin 500 mg twice a day for the diabetes, and levothyroxine 100 micrograms every morning for my thyroid. I've also been on omeprazole 20 mg once a day for indigestion for years. And I take ibuprofen 400 mg, most days, for my shoulder — I buy that from the chemist myself.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Yes, codeine makes me very sick, so I avoid it. That's the only one I know of.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?

Yes, I'm struggling to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings now — that's the thing that worries me most. He's got Parkinson's and I'm his main carer, so I don't know what I'd do if I can't keep it up.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes, that's my real worry — that I won't be able to keep looking after my husband. He depends on me for everything, and if I run out of steam I don't know who'd step in.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
